x: …lker went away to win with Davidson and Tooby 2nd and 3rd respectively. The Junior half mile was much more exciting and Stevens scored from Payne with Tupper third.…

The long jump held by candlelight, proved a win for Percy Luxon with 21ft. 9ins. and I understand Mal Ash surprised himself by jumping 19ft. 4ins. It seems we lost the match through lack of juniors although Stevens and Bowman ran in the 880 yards, but were unplaced.
Stevens won the Junior 880 in 2m. 7.8s. with D.

Out of the many eligible lads who could have run, only four in fact did so - a very poor entry. Right from the start it was a two man battle between Dabbs and Stevens, and the former had to pull out his best to win.
Stevens ran a very steady race, and hung on grimly in the closing stages, when obviously very tired, to be our second man home, 143rd, a fine performance in a big field.
John had the dubious pleasure of running solo knowing that Ellis (T.V.H.) Stevens (Reading) and Johnston (Portsmouth) were fighting it out behind.
In the Berkshire Championships at Maidenhead DICK PIOTROWSKI split the Stevens brothers of Reading AC to finish an excellent 2nd. Meredith and Merriman, also of Reading, were a minute down.
Despite being without the Stevens brothers, Merriman and MacAndrew, Reading proved easy winners and established themselves as a serious threat to our Southern & National teams.
Fastest times: Badgery (Mit) 16:51, Lightfoot (Read) 16:55, Stevens (Read) 17:02. CRANFORD (Thames Valley Harriers)---March 22nd
Carrying on the good work, Trevor got past Stevens (TVH) and made ground on Wainer (Hillingdon), all three of them increasing their lead over the next few clubs.
